player.name: Brother Ambrose Hake
player.concept: A disgraced former temple bookkeeper. Heavy drinker, and has a nose for trouble. Smelt one too many things he shouldn't have, and was let go on the pretense of being a drunk (which he absolutely was)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The wharf falls quiet behind Hobb’s retreating lantern. Ahead, the Heron’s hoist swings sacks down into the broad barge; grain dust drifts through the light leaking between the boards. Saul pushes himself up from his brazier to begin his round, while Duchess snores across the land-door threshold. The river door lies along the slick plank walk, its grille dark.

Kell stands at your side, watching the old watchman. “I’ll stay where I can see who comes and goes,” she says. “Unless you want a witness inside.” In your palm, Hobb’s brass token is cold and greasy. The midnight bell is close.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: No you stand watch. I'll head inside (walks up to Saul)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Kell stops where she is, taking up a position with a clear view of the land door. “I’ll stand watch, investigator,” she says. Her pencil rests against the closed notebook.

Saul turns at your approach, lifting his lantern. Duchess remains asleep across the threshold, one heavy paw twitching in a dream. “Who goes there?” he calls. “Speak up, and all’s well.” His right ear angles toward you. “You’re the King’s investigator, then?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: I suppose that describes me fairly well. Who might you be?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
“Saul Tench,” he says, raising his lantern a little. “Watchman here, and all’s well.” His gaze flicks to Kell, standing watch down the wharf, then back to you. Duchess snores between you and the wicket.

“On a loading night, the land door’s for the Master,” Saul adds, louder than the dark requires. “The gang use the river grille and a brass token. Orders are orders, and all’s well.” He watches to see what you’ll do.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: who's this Master you keep referring to?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Saul shifts his lantern from your face to the brass token in your hand. “Master Sallow,” he says, then turns his right ear toward you. “Palace gentleman. Silver-topped cane. Lavender enough to announce him before his lantern-boy does.” His mouth tightens briefly. “He comes at midnight. I hold the wicket, Duchess keeps off his ankles, and all’s well.”

Duchess gives a damp snort without waking. Saul looks down at her, then back to you. “That’s the Master. The land door’s still for him.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Who are the poeople inside?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text: “Inside?” Saul shifts his lantern toward the warehouse. “Hep and her porters on the sacks; Hobb on the hoist; Mister Scrope up in his glass box with the book. All working, and all’s well.” He rubs his hands over the brazier. “The gang come through the river grille with a token. Land door’s for the Master.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Land door?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
“The land door,” Saul repeats, turning his right ear toward you. “This one. For the Master, at midnight. The gang use the river door.” He taps the wicket with his lantern handle; the door stays barred.

Duchess snores across the threshold. Behind you, Kell keeps watch without moving. The brass token rests in your hand; the river entrance is along the plank walk, beyond the warehouse’s shadow. Saul waits by the brazier, watching you.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Well I was told to meet the master here. He gave me this token.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Saul eyes the token, then your face. “The Master gave you the token?” He repeats it loudly, turning his right ear toward you. “A buyer, then?” His gaze flicks toward Kell, still watching the door.

Duchess wakes, lifts her heavy head, and sniffs at your hand. The brass smells of Hobb and the warehouse; she gives a low, uncertain rumble. Saul’s fingers tighten around his lantern handle. “That token’s for the river grille. The land door is still the Master’s.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Aight well where do I have to go?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Saul points down the wharf, toward the dark strip of planks running beside the warehouse over the water. “River door. Along the plank walk, down at the waterline. Show the brass token at the grille and someone inside draws the bolt.”

Duchess sniffs your hand once more, then settles her head on her paws, still awake. Saul keeps his lantern trained on you. “That’s where the gang goes in. Not the land door. And all’s well.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: (I follow his directions along the plank walk)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The plank walk clings to the warehouse piles above the fast black river. It’s slick underfoot, and the hoist swings overhead as sacks descend toward the Patience. Through gaps in the tarred boards, lanternlight catches the gang at work: wheat-ear sacks split open, grain poured into heron-marked ones.

At the waterline, the river door’s grille is shut. As you approach, movement stirs inside; someone comes near the other side. The brass token is ready in your hand. A voice calls through the grille: “Hobb? You’re late.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: *I walk up to the man

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The figure on the far side of the grille is a porter in grain-white, broad-shouldered and flour-dusted. His eyes drop to the token in your hand; he doesn’t reach for the bolt.

“Not Hobb,” he says. “Who are you, then?” Beyond him, the hoist creaks, and a sack swings over the dark water.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Was sent here. Told there's some mechendise I might be interested in. Was given this (presents the coin thing Hobb gave me)

transcript.speaker: dice
transcript.text: Persuasion check to talk your way into the Heron: 2 + 0 = 2 vs DC 13: failure

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The porter studies the token, then your face. “That’s Hobb’s,” he says. He keeps his hand off the bolt. “And you said the Master gave it to you.”

The grille stays shut. Inside, he turns his head toward the floor and calls, “Hep! Someone’s at the door with Hobb’s token, says he’s come for the Master.”

Hobb pauses on the hoist. Across the gap, the porter keeps his eyes on you now, wary and watchful. The token has got you recognized—not admitted.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Well Hobb gave it to me. Technically didn't get it directly from the master. Said it would get me into the heron.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The porter’s suspicion eases a fraction. “Hobb gave it to you?” He glances past you toward the hoist. Hobb is watching from the ropes, his wrapped hand held close. For a moment he meets your eye, then looks away.

From inside, Hep Grist’s winch-voice cuts through the creak of the hoist. “If he’s come to talk, he can do it while he works. We’re short a pair of hands.” The porter unbolts the grille just enough to look you over. “You carrying anything heavier than a token?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Sure I suppose I can lend you a hand. Will give me a good oportunity to peruse.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The porter gives a short nod and pulls the grille wide enough for you to pass. “Then take a sack. Mind your feet.”

You step onto the warehouse floor. Grain dust hangs in the lanternlight; the gang are slitting wheat-ear sacks and pouring their contents into heron-marked ones. Hep Grist looks you over once. “There. Hands, not talk. Take that to the chute.”

Hobb watches from beside the hoist, his wrapped hand tucked close. He says nothing, but his eyes linger on the token. Hep points to a full sack waiting by the stacks. “Lift.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: (I do as I'm told and make no immediate move to talk to hobb. Once they stop watching to eagerly I casually move closer and wait for him to give me the scoop)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
You shoulder the sack to the chute. Grain rasps inside it; around you the gang keep their heads down and their hands moving. When you drift closer to Hobb, he goes rigid at the hoist, eyes fixed on the rope.

Then lavender reaches the floor ahead of its owner.

The land door opens. Master Sallow enters with a lantern-boy and the two Crakes. Saul holds the wicket; Duchess rises with a growl. Hep’s gang work faster, quieter. Up in the counting-box, Scrope stands, one hand still on the open green ledger.

Sallow’s gaze sweeps the floor and settles on the sacks. “Forewoman. The count, if you please.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: (I look around the room to assess the chain of command. Who here is pressganged, who's hired muscle, and who's loyal to the gang)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
From the plank walk, you take in the room through the open river door. The six in grain-white work under Hep’s eye, moving quickly and speaking little. Hobb is by the hoist, his bandaged hand held close; he looks frightened, not like a man eager for a fight.

Sallow’s two Crakes are hired muscle: one talks, the other doesn’t. Both are moving off from Sallow toward the floor. Above them, Scrope stands over the open green ledger, one hand planted on it.

“Forty received,” Scrope murmurs to Sallow. “Forty entered against the Granary Roll numbers. Your initials are on the prior pages, sir.”

Sallow’s lavender-scented attention turns toward the counting-box.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: (I keep a low profile but an open ear)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
From the plank walk, you keep your head down and listen over the creak of the hoist.

“Forty received, forty entered,” Scrope murmurs. “Against the Granary Roll numbers, as recorded. The prior pages bear your initials, sir.”

Sallow’s cane taps once on the floor. “And tonight’s count?”

“Not yet complete, sir.”

Hep calls out a number, and the gang answer with the rasp of sacks and needles. Hobb stays by the hoist, his wrapped hand held close, eyes lowered. Sallow turns toward Scrope’s glass-sided box. “Then we shall not pretend the count is complete.” The green ledger remains open beneath Scrope’s hand.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: (I try and ask Hobb what's going on)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Hobb glances toward Sallow, then back to the hoist rope. His voice comes low, almost lost beneath the work.

“Master’s checking the count. Same as every loading night, sir.” His bandaged hand tightens around the rope. “I can’t talk now.”

The Crakes are moving through the floor, and Sallow stands below the counting-box while Scrope guards the open ledger. Hobb keeps his eyes down. “Not with him here.”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: (I try and work my way around to get a view of the ledger discreetly)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
You edge along the plank walk, keeping to the river door’s shadow. Through the grille, the floor is busy enough that your movement draws no immediate call—though the Crakes have spread out, and one stands between you and the counting-box stairs.

Scrope’s voice carries from above the sacks. “The count is forty received, forty entered against the Granary Roll numbers. The prior pages bear your initials, sir.” Sallow turns his face toward the clerk. The ledger lies open beneath Scrope’s hand; from here, you can see the green cover and the brass clasp, but not the writing.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: (I get a bit closer to have a closer look)

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
You ease closer to the grille. Inside, Scrope adjusts the open ledger under his hand, careful not to smudge the page. “For completeness, sir,” he murmurs, “the entries identify each wagon by its Granary Roll number. The matching receipts are here; the sale and your share follow. Your initials are against every page.”

Sallow’s expression goes still. “The count, Clerk.”

“Of course, sir.” Scrope’s hand remains on the book. The Crake nearest the river door turns his head toward you.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Oh uh hi there. Business doing good?

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
The Crake gives you a flat look. “Business is excellent,” he says. “Forty sacks, forty entries. The work’s keeping us from discussing it.”

From the counting-box, Scrope’s pen pauses. Sallow turns at the exchange, lavender trailing him even here. “Who is this, exactly?” he asks, mild as a man querying an invoice. The Crake stays between you and the stairs. The river door remains open behind you; Hobb grips the hoist rope a few feet away, silent.

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Just an extra pair of hands to help out.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Sallow looks you over as if checking a line on a form. “An extra pair of hands,” he says. “I was under the impression the hands were already accounted for.”

The talking Crake shifts to block the open river door more fully. Sallow’s eyes move to the token in your hand, then to Hobb at the hoist. Hobb goes very still.

“Porter,” Sallow says, calm and courteous. “Who admitted this man?” His gaze settles on Hep across the floor. “And why is he not working?”

transcript.speaker: player
transcript.text: Do you know how heavy these sacks are? I've been loading them all night.

transcript.speaker: gm
transcript.text:
Sallow’s eyes narrow slightly. “I should hope so, Porter. They are not intended to be carried for their own amusement.”

Hep answers before the Crake can. “I put him to work, Master. We’re short-handed, and he’s carried a sack to the chute.” She snaps her fingers toward the stacks. “Then keep carrying. We have a count to finish.”

Sallow’s gaze stays on you a moment longer, measuring the answer against the token and Hobb’s silence. “Very well. Forewoman, the count.” The Crake remains by the river door, blocking the way to the stairs.

history.summary:
Previous scene, "The Hanged Clerk", ended: Murder by persons unknown (hanged-clerk: open-case).
Brother Ambrose Hake leaves the yard with Prout’s death recorded as murder by persons unknown. The case is open, and Prout is being taken to the watch-house cold room, not the suicides’ pit. No one has been identified as responsible.

- **Ambrose:** In the yard with Kell, Cob, Moll, and Tull as the scene ends. He has learned that Prout had a thin mark distinct from the hoist burn, swelling at the back of his head, and clean palms. The cause and sequence of those injuries remain uncertain.
- **Cob:** Near Moll and the open board, wary but somewhat reassured after Kell agreed to protect the children from being taken to the Mending House. He said he heard two men with a lantern arguing with Prout a little after midnight. One wanted “the page”; then came a thump, a choking noise, and the hoist creaking. He hid until morning. His left boot crackles; he refused Ambrose’s request to inspect it.
- **Moll:** With Cob. She said she was across the lane in the cart shed and was not present when Prout died. She is guarded and protective of Cob.
- **Kell:** Beside the body when she ordered it taken to the cold room. She has recorded the death as murder by persons unknown and is willing to stand behind that decision, but has named no culprit.
- **Tull:** At the yard with the Captain’s order, which directed the death to be closed as self-murder at the request of Master J. Sallow of the Royal Purveyor’s office. He held the cart when Kell ordered it and sent the constables to take Prout to the cold room.
- **Promise:** Ambrose still owes Cob a hot dinner. Cob agreed to crawl inside for that dinner; the body was ultimately brought down by Ambrose shooting through the hoist rope.
- **Unresolved:** The two men, the “page,” the boot’s crackle, and Master Sallow’s role have not been explained.
lastMoments: Brother Ambrose Hake (player): Kell, I'm worried. Can you protect these kids until we get to the bottom of this?

Kell’s gaze settles on Cob, still crouched behind Moll. “Yes. I can keep the watch from taking either of you to the Mending House. I can’t promise what a gentleman may try.”

Moll’s face stays guarded, but her fist loosens slightly. Kell turns to Tull. “Hold the cart. I’m taking Prout in as a murder by persons unknown. The boy has given an account that needs recording.”

Tull puts his helmet back on. “Yes, Sarge.” He signals the constables to wait. Kell opens her notebook and looks to you. “I can stand behind that, investigator. I can’t write a name yet.”
Brother Ambrose Hake (player): Cob, you'll be safe. Can you tell me exactly what you heard and saw?

Cob’s shoulders ease a fraction. “Two men. A little after midnight. Lantern. Mister Prout argued with them. One wanted ‘the page.’ Then a thump, and a choking noise. The hoist creaked after. No sacks on it.” He looks down at his boots. “Cob hid till morning.”

Kell writes one line and underlines it. “Prout’s death: murder by persons unknown.” Tull signals the constables; they bring the cart for the body, under a sheet, to the watch-house cold room—not the pit. Kell closes her notebook. “An open case beats a wrong one, investigator.”

history.summary:
Previous scene, "The Drowned Rat", ended: Hobb goes to work (drowned-rat: gone-to-work).
Ambrose is at the top of the wet river stairs with Hobb’s brass Heron token in hand. Hobb has gone toward the Heron without it; he knows Ambrose has it and fears the Master will notice. Kell has not arrested him. The Rat’s game is unfinished, and the message Kell could send to the Marshal remains unwritten.

- Hobb admitted he held Prout in the loft and held the rope. He says he was coerced; he has not named the Master or explained the “page.”
- Hobb said his mother is upstairs over a tripe-dresser’s in the Shambles. The Master knows where she lives and has asked after her.
- Hobb said the token opens the Heron’s river grille. He is due there for night work; the Master comes at midnight.
- Ambrose told Hobb he would keep his mother safe and suggested he lay low, but no safe place or protection was arranged. Hobb said he could not leave his mother alone and went to work.
- Kell said she could record Hobb’s cooperation and speak for him, but could not guarantee what the King would do. She refused to make her home a secret safe house.
- Cob is at the Rat with his hot stew. He said he knows no suitable safe place and refused to involve himself or take Ambrose to Hobb’s mother.
- Cob’s left boot still crackles; he remains wary and has refused inspection. Ambrose’s earlier dinner promise to Cob has been paid.
- Hobb seemed frightened and burdened by his mother’s danger; Kell was concerned but firm, and Cob was protective and wary.
lastMoments: Brother Ambrose Hake (player): *I take the token and wish Hobb the best of luck*

The brass token is cold and greasy in your hand. Hobb gives you a small, tired nod from beside the door.

“Thank you, sir,” he says. “I hope you can keep your word.”

Then he turns and climbs into the dark, toward the wharves and the Heron. Kell watches him go, but doesn’t move to stop him.

“He knows you have the token,” she says quietly. “If the Master sees him arrive without it, he’ll know something’s wrong.”

Behind you, Cob holds his stew bowl close. The game sits unfinished; your cards remain face down before you.
Brother Ambrose Hake (player): Kell, what do we do? We can't just leave this man to his fate.

Kell looks toward the door Hobb has gone through. “We can’t make his choices for him, investigator. But we can still stand behind the promise you made.”

Outside, Hobb’s broad back descends the wet river stairs toward the wharves, his lantern swinging in the dark. You are at the top of the steps with the brass token in your hand.

opening: An hour or so after the Rat, near midnight, you and Kell reach the dark wharf with the Heron in view. Lantern light seeps through the cracks, grain dust swims in it, and the hoist swings sacks down into the barge. Saul’s brazier glows by the land door, Duchess snores across the threshold, and the river runs high and black. Hobb has gone inside to work; you have his brass token. Sallow is not here yet. A watchman heaves himself up to begin his round, leaving you a moment to choose your approach.
lead: Kell walks with you toward the Heron, where Hobb went after leaving the Rat; the token in your hand may get you through its river door, and the loading may hold proof of where the King’s grain goes. The last of the Rat’s noise falls behind you as midnight draws near.
